tagline: When matching endings make the eye forget
definition: Similarity of endings in neighboring words or phrases, used as a rhetorical sound pattern; in textual transmission, the term also describes omission caused by a copyist's eye skipping between similar endings.
etymology: From Greek homoioteleuton, having a similar ending, built from homoios, similar, and a form related to teleutē, ending or completion.

sections.heading: An ending the ear expects
sections.text: Neighboring phrases can acquire a family resemblance through recurring endings. “We seek clarity, stability, and accountability” uses related terminal sounds to gather distinct aims into one cadence. Homoioteleuton need not obey the meter or exact matching demanded by a particular tradition of rhyme.

sections.heading: An ending the eye mistakes
sections.text: A copyist looks away from an exemplar to write, then returns to find the last remembered ending. If another line ends similarly, the eye may land there instead. The intervening material disappears even though the surviving text can appear unusually smooth and plausible.

sections.heading: Ornament and accident
sections.text: The rhetorical figure normally involves arrangement; the textual error involves a failure of placekeeping. One makes repetition audible, the other lets repetition conceal loss. Their shared name identifies a perceptual resemblance without implying that a copying mistake secretly functions as an intentional literary technique.

sections.heading: Reading the absent middle
sections.text: Editors suspect such an omission when a shorter witness has corresponding terminal material around a plausible gap. Similar endings alone do not prove the history of an error. Manuscript relationships, grammar, sense, and independent witnesses must support any proposed reconstruction of the missing passage.

literary: The copyist's candle shivered, the twin endings beckoned, and between their courteous likenesses a kingdom vanished, leaving the chronicle smooth as snow above a fallen bridge.
art_caption: Five repeated terminals organize a cadence; a skipping arc bypasses a missing span, converting resemblance into omission.
